mainKeyword: self-emptying robot vacuum and mop combos
guideTitle: Best Self-Emptying Robot Vacuum and Mop Combos (2026)
metaTitle: Best Self-Emptying Robot Vac and Mop Combos
metaDescription: Six self-emptying robot vacuum and mop combos compared on dock design, bag versus bagless, hands-free intervals, suction and mop features.
expertTake: The Roborock Qrevo S Pro is the pick for a household that wants the dock to handle emptying, mop washing and drying in one place, and the Roborock Q7 M5+ is the value pick for a bag-based dock with a very long interval. Anyone who vacuums a small apartment a few times a week does not need a self-emptying dock and can save the money.
introParagraphs: A self-emptying dock moves the worst chore in robot ownership from the robot to a base. Every time the machine returns to charge, the base sucks the bin empty into a sealed bag or a bagless canister, and the robot is ready to run again without you touching it.

The convenience comes with new details to judge: how big the dock's bin is, whether it uses bags you must buy, how loud the emptying cycle is, and what the dock does about the mop. Those details decide whether the dock earns its footprint or becomes one more appliance to maintain.

products.name: Roborock Qrevo S Pro Robot Vacuum and Mop, 18,500 Pa, Multifunction Dock
products.description:
The Qrevo S Pro is the most complete machine in the group because its dock does everything: it empties the dust bin, washes the mop pads with 167 degree F water and dries them. That final step is the one that stops a damp mop from smelling by the next afternoon.

Suction is rated at 18,500 Pa, and a zero-tangle roller aimed at long hair keeps the brush from wrapping. The cost is the dock, which is large and has to sit against a wall with clearance around it, and it needs a water tank filled and emptied. Against the Q7 M5+, which uses a smaller dock and a simpler mop, it is the premium option.

Plan for the upkeep that comes with a wet dock. Empty the dirty-water tank regularly, wipe the mop wash tray and replace the dust bag when full. If you rent or have a small space, a dock this big may be too much machine.
products.bestFor: A home with pets or long hair that wants the dock to handle emptying and mop care.
pros: Dock empties the bin and washes and dries the mop
167 degree F hot water mop wash
cons: Large dock needs wall space and clearance
Water tanks add refilling and emptying chores

products.name: Roborock Q7 M5+ Robot Vacuum and Mop, 10,000 Pa, 2.7L Dock Bag
products.description:
The Q7 M5+ pairs a 10,000 Pa robot with the RockDock Plus, whose 2.7 litre sealed bag the maker says lasts up to seven to nine weeks. That is a long gap between bag changes, and it is the headline reason to choose it over a bagless station.

It carries dual anti-tangle brushes that scrape hair off as they spin, which suits pet homes. The mop is simpler than the Qrevo's, so you wash or replace the pad yourself, and there is no hot-water cleaning. It is the practical middle: a self-emptying dock, a sealed bag and a mop that handles light wiping.

Bag cost is part of the deal, so check replacements are available before you buy. Empty the water tank, rinse the mop after use and keep the dock filter clean. For a first self-emptying robot, it makes a sensible entry.
products.bestFor: A home that wants a long bag interval and a simple dock.
pros: 2.7L bag lasts up to 7 to 9 weeks
cons: Mop is simpler and not self-washing
Replacement bags are an ongoing cost

products.name: Shark PowerDetect NeverTouch RV2820YE Robot Vacuum and Mop
products.description:
The Shark RV2820YE has a 60-day base and a set of five PowerDetect technologies aimed at finding hidden debris. NeverStuck lets the robot lift itself over thresholds and obstacles, which the maker says gives up to twice the coverage of a robot that gets stuck.

The NeverTouch base means you do not touch the dirty bin: it empties into a sealed capacity. Against the Roborock Q7 M5+ it is a shorter interval at 60 days versus seven to nine weeks, but it brings a well-known brand with wide service coverage.

Check the base bag availability and the dock filter schedule. Clear cords and small items before runs, and wipe the sensors monthly. It is a solid pick for a home with thresholds, rugs and cluttered floors.
products.bestFor: A cluttered home with thresholds and rugs where getting stuck is the worry.
pros: NeverStuck helps the robot climb thresholds and obstacles
cons: Shorter interval than the Q7 M5+ bag
Mop features are less elaborate than the Qrevo

products.name: D16S MAX Robot Vacuum and Mop, 18,000 Pa, Bagless 1.3L Station
products.description:
This model uses a bagless station: debris empties into a 1.3 litre canister rather than a disposable bag. The attraction is that there is no bag to buy, which removes an ongoing cost and the risk of a supply that dries up.

It pairs that with 18,000 Pa suction and 360 degree LiDAR for systematic cleaning and multi-floor maps. A bagless canister must be emptied by you, and doing so releases dust in your face unless you do it carefully outdoors. At 1.3 litres, it also fills sooner than the 2.7 and 3.5 litre bags.

Wash the canister filter regularly and let it dry fully. It is the machine for an owner who dislikes buying consumables and does not mind an occasional dusty chore.
products.bestFor: An owner who wants to avoid buying bags.
pros: Bagless station means no ongoing bag cost
cons: Canister must be emptied by hand
1.3L capacity fills sooner than bag docks

products.name: BOTLIFE Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, 75-Day Station, 6,000 Pa
products.description:
The BOTLIFE has the largest dock bag in the group at 3.5 litres, which the maker says is good for up to 75 days, and a battery rated for up to 180 minutes of continuous cleaning. That runtime lets it cover a large floor without stopping to recharge.

Its 6,000 Pa suction is the lowest here, and the robot has a 350 ml bin and a 340 ml water tank with four adjustable water levels. It is a capable mid-tier machine rather than a flagship, and its suction will lag the Roborock models on thick carpet.

Check the long-term availability of bags and the brand's service terms, since this is a lesser-known name. Empty the water tank after each mopping run and keep the sensors clean.
products.bestFor: A large single-floor home that values runtime and a big dock bag.
cons: 6,000 Pa is the lowest suction here
Lesser-known brand with less support history

products.name: Kilgone Robot Vacuum and Mop Combo, Auto-Empty Base, 3.6 In. Tall
products.description:
The Kilgone stands only 3.6 inches tall, so it slides beneath low sofas and beds that block taller robots. A 2.5 litre sealed bag in the base collects debris for weeks, and two brushes are designed to resist hair wrap.

The low profile is the reason to buy it, because dust collects where larger robots cannot reach. It does the usual vacuum-and-mop job without a flagship dock, so the mop is simple and the dock does not wash it.

Check the bag supply and the brush condition regularly. It suits an apartment with low furniture.
products.bestFor: An apartment with low furniture that blocks taller robots.
pros: 3.6 inch height fits under low furniture
cons: Mop is basic and not self-washing

buyingCriteria.explanation: A bag dock, as on the Roborock Q7 M5+ and BOTLIFE, seals dust away and you throw the bag out every few weeks, but you must keep buying bags. A bagless station like the D16S MAX saves the bag cost but makes you empty a canister by hand. Think about whether you mind the dust more than the cost.

Makers quote 60 days for the Shark, up to 75 for the BOTLIFE and seven to nine weeks for the Q7 M5+. These are best-case numbers for light, dry debris. A house with pets, kids or a lot of carpet will fill a bag faster, so treat the figure as a ceiling. A bigger bag also means less frequent trips to the bin. Real intervals depend on what you vacuum: fine drywall dust and pet fur pack densely and fill a bag in weeks, while a tidy flat with hard floors can go far beyond the quoted time. The best habit is to check the bag window or app notice once a month and change it when it is about three quarters full, not when the robot starts to complain.

buyingCriteria.criterion: What the dock does with the mop
buyingCriteria.explanation: Only the Qrevo S Pro washes and dries the mop in the dock with 167 degree F water. On the others, the pad is wiped or replaced by hand. If you mop weekly, a dock that cleans the pad stops odour and saves a chore, but it adds tanks to fill and empty. Without a washing dock, you will pull the pad off, rinse it and let it dry yourself, which is no worse than a hand mop but is the chore that most owners eventually stop doing. A damp pad left on the robot or in the dock grows odour within a day, so the dock that dries the pad solves a problem that cheaper machines simply hand back to you.

Suction numbers climb every year: the Qrevo S Pro quotes 18,500 Pa, the D16S MAX 18,000 and the BOTLIFE 6,000. The difference matters more on carpet than on hard floor. Brush design and the robot's ability to lift the mop on carpet matter as much as the headline figure.

LiDAR, as on the D16S MAX, maps a room accurately even in the dark. The Shark's NeverStuck helps it climb thresholds and obstacles. A robot that gets stuck every day defeats the point of a self-emptying dock, so judge obstacle handling as seriously as suction.

Docks are big, and the Qrevo S Pro dock is the biggest. They need a wall, clear space on both sides and a power outlet, and a full water dock is heavy. Measure the spot before buying and leave room for the robot to dock without bumping. Place the dock away from stairs and on a hard floor, since a dock on a rug can slide when the robot pushes in, and make sure the Wi-Fi signal reaches that corner so the robot can report its status. A dock tucked behind a door that gets closed will leave the robot stranded.

howWeEvaluated.title: Dock capability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared what each dock does: empty only, or empty plus mop wash and dry. The Qrevo S Pro dock does everything, and the others empty only.

howWeEvaluated.title: Interval and consumables
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed claimed hands-free days against bag costs. The BOTLIFE 75 days and Q7 M5+ seven to nine weeks lead, and the bagless D16S MAX removes bag cost.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning power
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared suction figures and brush design. The 18,500 Pa Qrevo and 18,000 Pa D16S MAX lead, and anti-tangle brushes earned credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Navigation and clearance
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered LiDAR, obstacle climbing and height. The Shark NeverStuck and Kilgone 3.6 inch height stand out.

cards.label: Bag dock
cards.text: The Roborock, Shark, BOTLIFE and Kilgone docks seal dust in a disposable bag. They keep dust out of your face and last weeks, but bags are an ongoing cost.

cards.label: Bagless station
cards.text: The D16S MAX empties into a 1.3 litre canister. There is no bag to buy, but you must empty and wash the canister, and it fills sooner.

howToChoose.note: Bag docks for allergy-prone households, bagless for those who hate consumables. A sealed bag keeps dust and dander away from your nose at the moment of disposal, which matters if anyone in the house has asthma. A bagless canister is cheaper to run but turns each emptying into a small dust event, so empty it outdoors or into a bag held tightly around the opening.

rows: Hot water wash in the dock

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Look for a long bag interval, strong anti-tangle brushes, good obstacle handling and a mop that does not need babysitting. A self-emptying dock only saves time if the robot rarely gets stuck.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Qrevo S Pro handles the most chores, the Q7 M5+ has the longest bag interval and the Shark has the best obstacle handling.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: Spend more if you mop weekly or have pets; the Qrevo S Pro dock washes and dries the mop and manages hair. A dock that cleans the mop saves the chore people dislike most.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Save if you mostly vacuum hard floors. The Roborock Q7 M5+ or BOTLIFE empties itself and cleans well without a premium dock.

maintenance.interval: When full or every few weeks
maintenance.why: A full bag cuts emptying suction and can overflow. Replace it before it is stuffed.
Fine dust clogs the dock filter and reduces emptying power. Tap it clean or replace it.
Dust on sensors causes bumping and failed docking. Wipe with a dry cloth.
Hair wraps around bearings even on anti-tangle designs. Cut it free to protect the motors.
Stale water smells and grows slime. Rinse the tanks and mop pads and let them dry.

faq.q: Is a self-emptying dock worth it?
faq.a: For a home that runs the robot daily, yes: it turns weekly bin emptying into a bag change every month or two. For a small apartment run a few times a week it is less necessary.

faq.q: How long does a dock bag last?
faq.a: Makers quote 60 to 75 days or seven to nine weeks, based on light use. A pet home or carpeted house will fill it sooner, so check it monthly.

faq.q: Do I have to buy bags?
faq.a: Bag docks need replacement bags, which are an ongoing cost. A bagless station avoids that but needs you to empty the canister.
Most robots mop hard floors only and lift or detach the mop on carpet. Check the lift height for your rugs, and keep wet mopping away from unsealed wood.

faq.q: Why does my robot keep getting stuck?
faq.a: Cords, socks, thresholds and loose rug edges are the usual causes. Clear the floor and use no-go zones in the app. A robot like the Shark with NeverStuck helps.

faq.q: How noisy is the emptying cycle?
faq.a: Dock emptying is loud for 10 to 20 seconds, because it uses a strong vacuum. Schedule runs so that the cycle does not fall during calls or sleep. Most apps let you set a quiet window, and the robot will wait until the window ends before it returns to empty, which is the cheapest noise fix available. Placing the dock on a rug or a rubber mat also dampens the rattle through the floor.
